title: Derived stalk of an oriented direct image is Milnor-tube cohomology
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ and $g:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring. Use small etale topoi [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and their left oriented product $P=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Put $Z=X\times_SY$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\psi_{f,g}:Z_{\mathrm{Et}}\to P$ be the geometric morphism specified by the two projections and their equality over $S$; on a site triple $(U\to V\leftarrow W)$ its inverse image is the sheaf represented by $U\times_VW$. Let $x,y$ be geometric points [def-weil-geometric-point] of $X,Y$, and choose a specialization $c:g(y)\to f(x)$, meaning a morphism $S_{(g(y))}\to S_{(f(x))}$ of $S$-schemes between their strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], equivalently the corresponding $2$-morphism of geometric points in the convention of [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. Let $z:\mathbf{Set}\to P$ be the resulting point. The composite $Y_{(y)}\to S_{(g(y))}\xrightarrow{c}S_{(f(x))}$ defines $M=X_{(x)}\times_{S_{(f(x))}}Y_{(y)}$, with its natural map $r:M\to Z$. For every bounded-below complex $K\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ of sheaves of constant $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], there is a canonical isomorphism in $D^+(\operatorname{Mod}\Lambda)$
$$z^*R\psi_{f,g,*}K\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(M_{\mathrm{Et}},r^*K).$$
Here $R\psi_*$ and $R\Gamma$ are total right derived functors, computed by K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and $r^*$ is exact derived inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image]. The displayed isomorphism is induced by restriction from the affine pointed triple neighbourhoods of $z$ to their inverse limit $M$, and is natural in $K$.

source.place: Illusie, Around the Thom--Sebastiani theorem, section 1.3, formula (1.3.1) and the preceding paragraph, printed p. 7 (PDF page 7); morphism psi and inverse-image formula in section 1.2, (1.2.1), printed p. 5. Read from work/illusie-nearby-cycles28.pdf. Local corroboration in literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, Expose XI: 1.4 (points of the oriented product), proof of Proposition 2.3 (fibre at a point as colimit over neighbourhoods (U -> V <- W)), and 4.3 (Psi^{-1}(U -> V <- W) = U x_V W).
